functional_sequences.title: Mucociliary clearance
functional_sequences.mechanism: Cilia propel hydrated surface mucus toward the larynx.
functional_sequences.scale_note: Sparse enlarged tufts and cell field; no quantitative mucus layer or beat frequency is rendered.

steps.label: Locate the clearance surface
steps.caption: The epithelial apical surface faces the airway. Its ciliated and secretory cells form one pseudostratified layer; nuclei at different heights do not create extra layers.

steps.label: Secretory cells provide mucus
steps.caption: Goblet-cell secretory compartments supply mucins at the apical surface. The airway surface also receives submucosal gland secretion. The displayed compartments are contents, not additional cell layers.

steps.label: Cilia act on the surface mucus
steps.caption: Effective and recovery strokes have a coordinated net proximal transport effect. Follow +model x toward the larynx; ciliary roots stay attached to the apical cells. The rest-shaped tufts indicate location only, not a measured beat waveform.

steps.label: Hydration preserves clearance
steps.caption: A hydrated periciliary brush of surface-tethered molecules separates surface mucus from the epithelial boundary. Mucus concentration can compress this region and impede clearance. Molecular brush and mucus rheology are explanatory text here, not represented meshes.

schematic_limitations: No beat motion, particles, mucus transport rate or cilium-level forces are simulated.
The periciliary compartment is not a simple empty water moat.
A continuous uniform mucus sheet is a teaching idealization, not asserted measured human tracheal topology.

functional_sequences.title: Gland secretion to the airway
functional_sequences.mechanism: Secretory acini and mucous tubules drain through collecting lumen and duct to epithelial outlet.
functional_sequences.scale_note: Six enlarged glands and 18 secretory units; representative density, cell spacing and lumen calibres.

steps.label: Find the in-wall glands
steps.caption: Secretory units remain in the submucosal wall. The supporting matrix is peeled in this view so the relation to airway and C-rings can be followed.

steps.label: Fluid and mucin enter gland lumens
steps.caption: Mucous cells deliver mucins; serous acini contribute fluid. CFTR-dependent cAMP-stimulated fluid secretion has been localized to the serous acinar region in isolated airway glands. This teaching sequence does not claim all secretagogues have identical CFTR dependence.

steps.label: Follow collecting route and duct
steps.caption: Trace the represented secretory lumen into the collector, then along the duct toward the surface. The open teaching face is a reversible removed closure. Visual continuity alone does not certify hydraulic continuity.

steps.label: Exit onto the airway surface
steps.caption: The duct reaches the epithelial outlet. Secretions join the surface material cleared proximally by cilia. Idealized serous acini and the retained demilune label do not mean every unit is a literal cap in three dimensions.

schematic_limitations: No CFD, ion flux, water transport or mucin exocytosis simulation.
Native view peels closure parts; intact anatomy is restored on reset.
Do not animate opaque tracer solids through gland cell cytoplasm.

functional_sequences.title: Posterior trachealis and the open C-ring
functional_sequences.mechanism: Transverse smooth-muscle bundles bridge the posterior cartilage interruption and can alter airway calibre.
functional_sequences.scale_note: Posterior gross compartment and enlarged representative spindle-cell field use different teaching scales.

steps.label: Identify the posterior interruption
steps.caption: Model -y is posterior. C-ring ends border the membranous wall; the trachealis bridges this posterior gap rather than making a complete circumferential muscular ring.

steps.label: Read transverse smooth-muscle organization
steps.caption: The gross carrier is peeled to expose spindle-cell samples and central nuclei. Muscle bundles run across the gap, transverse to model x. They have no skeletal-muscle striations.

steps.label: Understand coupled calibre change
steps.caption: Contraction changes the posterior wall shape and narrows the lumen while the cartilage and fibroelastic wall constrain it. Tissue geometry stays at rest here. A future deformation must move the coupled posterior mucosa and supporting tissues, not only the muscle.

schematic_limitations: No strain, contractile force, lumen-area change or attachment-preserving motion is generated.
No oesophageal bolus or cartilage collapse is simulated.
Transverse bundle direction follows the posterior arc; it is not a uniform Cartesian-axis morph of the whole muscle.

functional_sequences.title: Cough clearance context
functional_sequences.mechanism: An inspiratory preparation, pressure-generating compression and expulsive airflow help remove airway material.
functional_sequences.scale_note: Wall fragment supplies structural context only. Glottis, lungs, respiratory muscles and neural circuit are outside the specimen.

steps.label: Inspiratory preparation
steps.caption: Cough is a coordinated respiratory event. Inspired operating volume influences the subsequent peak cough flow; this isolated wall does not supply lung volume or an airflow boundary condition.

steps.label: Pressure-generating compression
steps.caption: Glottic closure and expiratory muscle activity are outside the wall specimen. Tracheal smooth muscle can be recruited during cough; the cited dog experiment found sustained contraction during mechanically induced cough, not a universal human phase curve.

steps.label: Expulsive clearance
steps.caption: When the glottis opens, expiratory airflow can shear and move mucus toward the larynx (+model x). Narrower area increases velocity only at a specified flow; actual cough flow depends on lung volume, pressures and dynamic airway behaviour.

steps.label: Return to structural context
steps.caption: The teaching stages return to the intact wall. Cough complements slower mucociliary transport. Stage duration is reading time and does not reproduce a cough cycle.

schematic_limitations: No glottis, chest-wall mechanics, intrathoracic pressure or patient cough waveform is represented.
No claim that trachealis contraction alone creates cough or invariably increases measured cough flow.
Neural recruitment evidence from dogs is species-limited.
